title: [Zero to ASIC] Apparently, You can Vibe-code analog radio circuits now.
gist: A SemiWiki forum post points to Matt Venn's demonstration of AI-assisted analog chip design (a 433 MHz radio on a Tiny Tapeout chip) and to the Razavi-Bench analog-reasoning benchmark, where the poster says Gemini 4 leads. The poster observes people moving away from extreme views on AI toward treating it as another valid tool.

insights.claim: Matt Venn's video shows AI-assisted analog chip design, with an explanatory page and a 3D web-based GDS viewer for a 433 MHz radio on a Tiny Tapeout chip.
insights.speaker: Jozo035
insights.so_what: Open-source tapeout tooling is lowering the barrier to analog experimentation.
insights.quote: A radio on a tiny open-source chip

insights.claim: Razavi-Bench is an expert-curated benchmark of whether frontier AI models can reason about analog circuit design, and the poster says Gemini 4 is leading right now.
insights.speaker: Jozo035
insights.so_what: Analog reasoning benchmarks give a measurable gauge of AI progress in a hard EDA niche.
insights.locator: There is also benchmark specialized in analog circuits

insights.claim: The poster sees more people abandoning extremely positive or negative positions on AI and accepting it as just another valid tool.
insights.speaker: Jozo035
insights.so_what: Sentiment around AI in chip design is normalizing, per one forum observation.
insights.quote: just accepting that it is just another valid tool
